changes.from: 2026-06-04 (Coachella City Council special meeting approved an interim urgency moratorium on data centers, per NBC Palm Springs and kvcrnews.org reporting); extended on or about 2026-07-09 while the city drafts a permanent ban
changes.to: 2026-06-04 (Urgency Ordinance 1229, as recited in the later city ordinance); city accounts record extension Ordinance 1230 adopted July 8, 2026.

changes.from: Consistent with the Gov. Code section 65858 interim urgency ordinance pattern already documented elsewhere in this inventory (initial up to 45 days, extendable to a 2-year maximum by 4/5 vote): reported as an initial temporary/urgency moratorium adopted 2026-06-04, then extended around 2026-07-09 ('Coachella Extends Temporary Ban On Data Center Developments,' Patch) as the council moves toward a permanent ban. Exact day counts and vote margins were not confirmed in the sources reviewed.
changes.to: Initial 45-day moratorium; city accounts record a July 8, 2026 extension for an additional 10 months and 15 days. Final operative wording of Ordinance 1230 and the moratorium endpoint remain unverified.

changes.from: Interim Urgency Ordinance No. 1229 (adopted 2026-06-04, 45-day pause); extended by Urgency Ordinance No. 1230 (adopted 2026-07-08/09, 10 months 15 days); superseded by Ordinance No. 1231, adding Chapter 17.92 to the Coachella Municipal Code to permanently prohibit data center uses citywide (first reading 2026-08-12, second reading/adoption 2026-08-26, effective 30 days after adoption).
changes.to: Urgency Ordinance 1229, followed by extension Ordinance 1230; later Ordinance 1231 adds Chapter 17.92 to prohibit data-center uses, with defined exclusions and accessory-use qualifications. The August 26 second-reading passage is supported by the city meeting record and linked revised attachment; that attachment has blank signature and vote fields. Formal termination of the temporary ordinances is not established.

changes.from: Public backlash and protests over a large proposed data center project and a power agreement with developer 'Stronghold'; council terminated the specific project and moved toward a permanent ban
changes.to: The city sought time to evaluate data-center impacts and whether uses should be regulated, restricted, or prohibited. Previously recorded specific-project and termination claims remain unverified in this source review.

changes.from: Replaced as of 2026-09-23. The City Council adopted Ordinance No. 1231 on 2026-08-26 (second reading), permanently prohibiting data center uses citywide (with limited exceptions for accessory server/IT rooms); effective 2026-09-25, thirty days after adoption. Mayor Figueroa has also voiced support for a future ballot measure to entrench the ban, but no such measure had been placed on a ballot as of this pass.
changes.to: The legacy replaced classification is retained as a historical inventory label pending lifecycle reconciliation, not a new finding of formal termination. The city meeting record supports August 26, 2026 second-reading passage of Ordinance 1231 after the moratorium study. Its thirty-days-after-adoption clause does not independently establish an operative September 25 date or a moratorium endpoint. Formal termination, overlap, publication, later actions and present force remain unresolved. [VERIFY]

changes.from: A large proposed data center project tied to a power agreement with 'Stronghold'; project reported terminated by the city (per NBC Palm Springs, 'Coachella City Council Halts Data Center Project, Cuts Ties with Stronghold,' 2026-06-05)
changes.to: Prior inventory reporting associates a proposed project and power agreement with Stronghold; project identity, status and legal applicability have not been independently verified in this review. [VERIFY]

changes.from: Moratorium adopted (Ord. 1229) and extended 10 months 15 days (Ord. 1230); superseded by a permanent citywide prohibition on data centers (Ord. 1231), adopted 2026-08-26 and effective 2026-09-25. Coachella is the first Coachella Valley city and second California city (after Monterey Park) to permanently ban data centers.
changes.to: City records support a historical policy succession from moratorium Ordinance 1229, as extended by 1230, to the adopted Ordinance 1231 prohibition. This does not establish formal repeal or termination of the pause, an exact endpoint, exclusive replacement, or current legal force.
